# Skills

The 4 skills SE loads, each by its name and when it is used; each guidance note is a skill too, listed with the rules.

| Skill | When it is used |
|---|---|
| `catch-up` | Catch up on a repository and drive it to a finished, committed state as SE. Use when: catching up, resuming after a break or handover, "where are we", "what is still open", "continue the work", "finish this", "get it to a finished state". Reads handover, git, issue and session history, turns every worktree-able package into a work issue with an independent worker session, files work for other repositories as issues there, presents user decisions and escalations with the decision skill, applies answers, has a dedicated integrator merge delivered pull requests (each carrying its field report), rebuild and release, and updates the handover. |
| `decision` | How every decision is made, the agent's own and those it brings to the person: one Obsidian Markdown note per decision that says how others solve its problem, a Pugh matrix in obs's `pugh` fence with the nine-item checklist, asked about the general mechanism rather than the single instance; its output is the answered artifact. Load it whenever you decide something that is not mechanical, or present a decision, an escalation or an open point to the person. |
| `update` | Update SE and everything the project relies on to the newest releases, across breaking releases too, then follow the upgrade guide between the versions: the one command SE's start report names, /se:update. Use when the person runs /se:update, says yes to the report's update line, or asks to update SE or the components; in a cloud session, as the first action after the start report. |
| `work-model` | The shared rules of how we work, for every role (SE, worker, integrator): one work issue in, a pull request out whose description is the field report; the box; escalation; freshness, dependencies and scheduling; worktrees; local tickets and notes; what a project provides. Load it whenever you act as SE, worker or integrator, write or read work or retro issues or field reports, or use <se>/scripts/work_tickets.py. |
